item.title: Self-Hosted API Fuzzing: RESTler vs Boofuzz vs APIFuzzer (2026)
item.description: API fuzzing is the practice of sending malformed, unexpected, or boundary-case inputs to API endpoints to uncover security vulnerabilities, reliability bugs, and edge-case failures. Unlike traditional API testing that validates expected behavior, fuzzing actively tries to break your API — finding injection points, buffer overflows, logic errors, and unhandled exceptions before attackers discover them in production.
